#4471 review · separate causes and unresolved timing symptoms

owner j3apyye investigated reviewed 2026-11-04 · 0 days ago

The exported version of the original incident described the merged reports as one parser problem with one fix queued. Its own computed table did not support that conclusion. The booking form’s hint and the shared parser are separate failure paths. Keeping them in one ticket can hide the form problem behind the parser’s queued fix.

This review uses the supplied export, not a live production investigation. Counts below come from the report IDs, tenant directory and executable classifier at render time. They measure report assignments; they do not prove the production cause of every report.

Reconcile the export

427 exported rows → 412 unique report IDs; 15 repeated overlap rows do not add reports. All 412 unique reports were merged into #4471.

The supplied classifier assigns 2 causes. Intake tags disagree with that classifier for 38 reports.

Reports arrived from 2026-04-01 through 2026-10-04. The largest merge day was 2026-07-02: 184 unique reports were merged that day.

The export’s pages overlap. Deduplicate by report ID before filtering to #4471, grouping, or drawing a timeline. Different IDs remain separate reports even when their words match. The browser’s locale and intake tag are guesses, not substitutes for the tenant directory.

5 reports flagged in the desk's oneDayMove notes; assigned to parser by tenant. Review their bodies before assuming a cause.

The ticket column reflects the supplied export, before this review’s GitHub filings.

Parser: day-first dates read month first. The shared-parser behavior described in src/lib/kb/causes.ts reads dates month first. For a tenant using day-first dates, 07/04/2026 intended as 7 April can become 4 July. Harbour Dental’s app reports R-41200 and R-41201 show this swap. Keep this problem in its own parser ticket. Use the parser row’s count above, including its explicitly marked exceptions.

Hint: booking-v3 tells people to enter the other order. For day-first tenants, booking-v3 prints MM/DD/YYYY, while its form reads dates in the tenant’s order. The form can therefore misread an entry even if the shared parser is fixed. Copper Studio’s form report R-41230 and Alder Physio’s form report R-41241 follow this path. File a separate form-hint ticket with the hint row’s count above.

The classifier uses Intl.DateTimeFormat to determine the tenant’s date order, then checks the report’s channel and the tenant’s form version. A booking-v3 tenant’s app or email report still follows the parser rule; the hint rule applies to its form reports. Do not count causes from intake tags or split them from subject lines alone.

Do not explain away the timing reports

5 reports are listed in the desk's oneDayMove notes. They remain included in their assigned cause's count; they are not extra reports.

reporttenant / channelreporter's wordsassigned cause
R-41202kettle.books / emailInvite says Tuesday 12 May. Calendar says Monday 11 May. My client turned up on the Monday. We had coffee.parser
R-41209alder.physio / appEvery booking in June is one day off. Only June. Why only June.parser
R-41236nine.lanterns / appThe invite arrived before I made the booking. I would like to know how.parser
R-41344pale.harbour / emailClient in Lisbon got Tuesday. Client in Toronto got Monday. Same meeting. We held it twice.parser
R-41620lantern.row / emailTuesday 6 October showed as Monday. I moved it myself. I have stopped reporting these but my colleague says it helps you.parser

The desk’s note label is broader than the words in the reports. R-41236 says the invite arrived before the booking; it does not actually describe a one-day move. R-41344 says people in Lisbon and Toronto saw different weekdays. A timezone explanation is plausible, but this export has no event instants, timezone settings or invite payloads to establish it.

R-41202, R-41209 and R-41620 describe day discrepancies that the month/day-swap example does not explain. Keep their IDs visible in the parser investigation and obtain the original entered date, stored timestamp, timezone, rendered invite and reproduction steps. Do not claim they are a proven shared third bug, subtract them silently, or count them twice.

R-41620 also says the reporter stopped reporting these failures. A smaller incoming count would therefore not, by itself, establish that the problem had been fixed.

The classifier assigns a cause from tenant and channel; it never reads the report body. Its result is useful routing evidence, not proof that contradictory symptoms are resolved.

The desk kept merging reports

The chart separates when reports arrived from when the desk merged them. A bulk merge is a desk action, not a sudden increase in product failures. Reports continued after the bulk merge; “known” did not mean resolved in this snapshot.

Keep the next reports separate

Use the updated triage guidance and replacement decision. Matching words can identify candidates to read, but cannot establish a common cause. Check tenant locale, form version, channel and the body before merging. Same-subject app and form reports from Alder Physio can belong to different problems; different-subject app and email reports from Kettle Books can belong to the same parser problem.

Unknown tenants and bodies that do not fit the supposed cause need investigation, not an automatic merge. Preserve report IDs and recompute the totals as the desk receives reports. Recheck the page after a fix or fresh export; these counts describe this snapshot only.
